basis: Mitochondrial spastic neuropathy; optic neuropathy occurs in 30-79%, with visual loss in 2/2. Muscle wasting is neurogenic rather than evidence of primary muscle damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle wasting and weakness reflect neuropathy; talipes can follow spasticity. Direct skeletal or muscle disease affecting at least 30% is not established.

basis: Acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency defines immune-mediated subcutaneous angioedema. Reversible bowel and airway edema does not establish lasting extra-cutaneous damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: episodic upper-airway edema can be severe but does not establish lasting airway damage; transient swelling is excluded.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: recurrent bowel-wall edema is reversible; abdominal attacks do not establish persistent gastrointestinal damage.

basis: Renal magnesium-wasting disorder; persistent psychomotor delay is described as typical, supporting an inferred frequency of at least 30%, although subtype frequencies are uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: involved: typical mild-to-moderate psychomotor delay supports persistent developmental impairment in an inferred >=30%; transient electrolyte-related symptoms alone would not qualify.

basis: Ectodermal dysplasia, oral clefting and intellectual disability characterize the syndrome. Eyelid fusion is optional in this definition, without an established >=30% frequency.

decisions.ocular: none: fused eyelids are an additional possible feature; the AEC parent alone does not establish their frequency or diagnostic necessity in this specific syndrome.

basis: Intellectual disability and characteristic ptosis define the syndrome; corneal disease supports ocular pathology. Hearing impairment occurs in 80-99%.

decisions.ocular: primary: characteristic ptosis is explicitly included in the syndrome definition and occurs in 80-99%; corneal disease and cataracts provide additional ocular evidence.

basis: Palmoplantar keratoderma establishes skin disease. Acrocyanosis occurs in 80-99% but does not demonstrate vascular injury or clinically important loss of vascular function.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: acrocyanosis is a defining vasomotor sign, but its 80-99% frequency does not establish vessel injury or damaging cardiovascular disease.

basis: Isolated LMNA cardiomyopathy with conduction disease. Lipodystrophy is a separately diagnosed laminopathy phenotype despite its 30-79% annotation; muscular dystrophy occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.dermatologic: none: lipodystrophy represents a separate LMNA-associated disorder; its 30-79% annotation does not establish fat loss caused by this isolated cardiomyopathy.

basis: Developmental disability, cardiac defects and skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; cardiac anomalies occur in 2/6. Nail aplasia occurs in 30-79%. Tumor predisposition adds no axis.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: absent fingernails and toenails are permanent structural losses of skin appendages, annotated frequent (30-79%).
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal anomalies, including clinodactyly, are explicitly part of the syndrome definition; clinodactyly and pes planus are annotated in 30-79%.

basis: Valine organic aciduria with defining cerebral anomalies. Microtia is a congenital external-ear defect occurring in 30-79%; hypogonadism shares the endocrine axis.

decisions.otologic: involved: microtia represents structural hypoplasia of the external ear, which this axis includes, and is annotated frequent (30-79%).

basis: Inflammation of the cerebrum establishes the neurologic axis. The generic definition does not establish infection, autoimmunity or another qualifying immune-mediated mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inflammation alone does not establish infection or immune-mediated disease; neither the definition nor the ancestors specify a qualifying mechanism.
